info.bio:
The Smashing Pumpkins es un grupo musical estadounidense de rock alternativo, formado en Chicago, Illinois, en 1988. Tras disolverse el 2 de diciembre de 2000, la agrupación anunció por medio de su sitio web oficial, el 20 de abril de 2006, una reunión y la grabación de un nuevo álbum.

The Smashing Pumpkins estaba compuesto originalmente por Billy Corgan (guitarra y voz), James Iha (guitarra), D'arcy Wretzky (bajo) y Jimmy Chamberlin (batería).

scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Nevermind de Nirvana (noviembre de 1991) llega al número uno el 11 de enero de 1992 y acaba con el reinado del lite metal. Los medios abrazan a Kurt Cobain y Eddie Vedder, las radios crean formatos «alternativos», la gran emisora de metal de Los Ángeles, KNAC, se vende en 1995 y MTV cancela Headbangers Ball en 1996; hasta Kerrang! se abre a la nueva moda, y los críticos, que crecieron con el rock universitario, ven por fin validado su gusto. El grunge no es metal aunque comparte la guitarra y la voz fuerte: alterna partes duras y suaves, canta el dolor y la desesperación, viste de tienda de segunda mano e identifica a la generación X con los débiles, frente al poder y el placer del metal («Somos pesados, pero no heavy metal», dice Krist Novoselic). Hacia 1998 el alternativo está moribundo.

scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

podcast.title: Debut Album Anticipation (1991)
podcast.body: During the filming of *Singles* in early 1991, The Smashing Pumpkins, despite being from Chicago, were still "a couple of months away from releasing their debut album." They were later associated with the grunge movement, highlighting the scene's growing influence beyond Seattle even before their major breakthrough. "And the smashing bumpkins, a group that would be sucked into the whole grunts thing even though they were from Chicago, was still a couple of months away from releasing their debut album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Singles Soundtrack Contribution (1992)
podcast.body: Songs from The Smashing Pumpkins were played on the radio and in alternative clubs throughout late 1992, following the release of *Singles*. The movie and its soundtrack were instrumental in expanding the reach and popularity of grunge music, even for bands like the Pumpkins who were not originally from Seattle. "Songs from Allison Chains, Pearl Jam, The Screaming Trees and The Smashing Pumpkins were all played on the radio and in alternative clubs."

podcast.title: Billy Corgan's Anti-Moshing Stance (1995)
podcast.body: In 1995, Billy Corgan publicly took a stand against moshing during a show in Chicago, expressing that such behavior was inappropriate and unfair to other audience members. This reflected a growing concern among bands about safety in mosh pits. "I and we publicly take a stand against mashing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Drug Overdoses and Jonathan Melvoin's Death (1996)
podcast.body: Within six weeks of the Smashing Pumpkins' 1996 World Tour beginning, drummer Jimmy Chamberlain and touring keyboardist Jonathan Melvoin overdosed on heroin in Thailand in February, and again in Spain in May, narrowly escaping death. Jonathan Melvoin was subsequently fired but remained with the band until the tour concluded, while Jimmy was placed on "double secret probation." On July 11, 1996, just before two sold-out shows at Madison Square Garden in New York, Jimmy and Jonathan went to the East Village to purchase "red rum," a highly potent form of heroin. At 4 AM the next morning, Jonathan, who was ironically trained as an emergency medical technician, died from an overdose. Jimmy awoke from his stupor and called the police, leading to official statements being given within hours. "Jonathan Melvoin O.D. on heroin in Thailand."

podcast.title: Drummer Firing (1996)
podcast.body: After the summer of 1996, drummer Jimmy Chamberlin was "fired for exceeding the allowable number of drug and discretion," which caused the "bottom end" of the band's sound to fall out, affecting the groove and swing of subsequent songs. "First Jimmy Chamberlain was fired for exceeding the allowable number of drug and discretion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dublin Concert Fatality (1996)
podcast.body: During their World Tour for *Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness*, The Smashing Pumpkins played to about 7,000 people at the Point Theatre in Dublin, Ireland, on May 11, 1996. Seventeen-year-old Bernadette O'Brien rushed into the mosh pit and was crushed. Singer Billy Corgan stopped the show twice, first asking the crowd to cease crushing, then at 10:00 PM announcing the gig was over due to O'Brien being "nearly dying." O'Brien died the next day from massive internal injuries caused by the crushing weight. Her friend and two cousins were also injured but recovered. "I'm sorry, we can't play on, the gigs are over. There's a girl who's nearly dying. We, as human beings, cannot play up here while people are getting hurt down there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jimmy Chamberlain's Firing and Return (1996-1999)
podcast.body: Five days after Jonathan Melvoin's death, Billy, James, and Darcy of The Smashing Pumpkins issued a statement announcing their decision to "sever our relationship with our friend and drummer Jimmy Chamberlain." They explained that for nine years they had "battled with Jimmy's struggles with the insidious disease of drug and alcohol addiction," which had "nearly destroyed everything we are and stand for," and confirmed they would "carry on without him." Jimmy was exiled from the band for three years, a period during which the Pumpkins' fortunes began to decline. In an effort to revitalize the band, Jimmy was eventually asked to rejoin, making his return on April 10, 1999, at St Andrews Hall in Detroit, where the band appeared in their familiar lineup for the first time since July 1996. "Today, we are very sorry to tell you that we've decided to sever our relationship with our friend and drummer Jimmy Chamberlain."

podcast.title: Jimmy Chamberlin's Dismissal (July 17, 1996)
podcast.body: Drummer Jimmy Chamberlin was formally dismissed from the band on July 17, 1996, following repeated drug-related incidents, including multiple overdoses with touring keyboardist Jonathan Melvoin, who died of an overdose on July 11. The band released a statement citing his "insidious disease of drug and alcohol addiction" that "nearly destroyed everything we are and stand for." "On July 17th, the band released this statement. Today, we are very sorry to tell you that we have decided to sever our relationship with our friend and drummer Jimmy Chamberlain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jonathan Melvoin's Overdose and Death (July 11, 1996)
podcast.body: Touring keyboardist Jonathan Melvoin, a heroin user, experienced multiple overdoses in 1996, including one in Bangkok on February 29 and another on May 2 where he and Jimmy Chamberlin were revived with adrenaline. Despite being fired, he was asked to finish the tour. On July 11, 1996, he and Chamberlin obtained a potent heroin called "Redrum" in the East Village and returned to the Regency Hotel, where Melvoin died of an overdose by 4 AM the following morning. "By 4 the following morning, Melvoin was dead of an overdose."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tragedy at Point Theatre (May 11, 1996)
podcast.body: During The Smashing Pumpkins' "Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness Tour" at the Point Theatre in Dublin, 17-year-old Bernadette O'Brien was crushed in a mosh pit and died from massive internal injuries. Billy Corgan halted the show, stating the band could not continue while people were getting hurt. This incident intensified the crackdown on moshing and led to increased legal repercussions. "And then on May 11th, 1996, something terrible happened."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Bassist Departure (1999)
podcast.body: About three years after Jimmy Chamberlin's firing, bass player D'Arcy Wretzky left the band. Her departure was "ostensibly to pursue an acting career," but she also had "drug issues." "About three years later, bass player Darcy Retsky left, ostensibly to pursue an acting career, but she had drug issues too."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Jimmy Chamberlin's Re-hiring and Tenure (1999-2000)
podcast.body: After a three-year absence, Jimmy Chamberlin was unexpectedly invited back to the band in 1999. He remained with The Smashing Pumpkins until their first breakup in December 2000. "Jimmy was out of the band for 3 years, but in 1999, he was invited back, which was something of a surprise."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Decision to Break Up (2000)
podcast.body: In October 2000, Billy Corgan made the decision to disband the Smashing Pumpkins. Despite their status as one of the most important, influential, and bestselling bands of the 1990s alternative nation, the band faced too many problems with their record label, management, and reportedly with guitarist James Iha, whom Corgan seemed to hold responsible for the ultimate breakup.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Final Concert at The Metro (2000)
podcast.body: The Smashing Pumpkins' final show was announced on October 17, 2000, and took place on December 2nd at The Metro in Chicago. This club held significant history for the band, as it was also the venue where they played their first proper gig on October 5, 1988. The farewell performance was an emotional night that lasted four long hours, serving as a "grand finale" to their career.

podcast.body: The Smashing Pumpkins played their final show around the turn of the millennium, which was seen as another disappointment and a sign of the struggles faced by the rock and alt-rock genres at that time. "The smashing pumpkins played their final show."

podcast.body: The band broke up after a "big lead up to one final show in Chicago" and remained broken up for six years. "And then a year after that, after a big lead up to one final show in Chicago, the band broke up and stayed that way for six years."

podcast.body: Billy Corgan retired The Smashing Pumpkins' name with a final concert in Chicago on this date. "Billy Corgan retired the name with a final show in Chicago in December 2nd of 2000."

podcast.title: Early Viral Online Marketing Campaign (2001)
podcast.body: *Machina, the Machines of God* was promoted with a "very cool viral online marketing campaign" in 2001, which was pioneering for its time. Fans were encouraged to decipher the album's weird themes, storylines, and mysteries. However, the campaign was abandoned before it was fully solved or finished. "And there was a very cool viral online marketing campaign that encouraged fans to figure out the weird themes and storylines and mysteries contained in the album and the artwork. Now remember, this was 2001. Nobody was doing this sort of thing back then."

podcast.body: Corgan vowed to bring the band back on the same day he released his solo album. "But then he vowed to bring the band back the same day he released his solo album which was June 25th, 2005."

"Well, let's call it a pseudo reunion that was essentially Billy Corgan and a rotating cast of people most fans never really got to know."

podcast.body: The band reunited in 2007, prompting questions about former members like D'Arcy Wretzky. "Dear Alan, with the reunion of the smashing pumpkins in 2007, it got me thinking, whatever happened to Darcy, the original bass player for the smashing pumpkins."

podcast.title: Tragedy at PNE Forum (September 24, 2007)
podcast.body: Another tragedy struck The Smashing Pumpkins when 20-year-old Kenny Leung died after being pulled unconscious from a mosh pit at their gig at the PNE Forum in Vancouver. Although an autopsy couldn't definitively link his death to crowd surfing or moshing, the incident reinforced the need for strict control over front-of-stage activities and fueled demands for a zero-tolerance policy against moshing. "On September 24th, 2007, 20-year-old Kenny Leung went to a pumpkin's gig at the P&E Forum in Vancouver."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Vancouver Mosh Pit Death (2007)
podcast.body: On September 24, 2007, 20-year-old Kenny Leung attended a Smashing Pumpkins concert at the P&E Coliseum in Vancouver. He was in the mosh pit when security pulled him out after noticing something was seriously wrong; he was unconscious but showed no obvious external injuries. An autopsy could not definitively link his death to crowdsurfing or moshing, leading investigators to conclude that "Something just went wrong while he was up front."

podcast.title: "Siamese Dream" Cover Models Reunion
podcast.body: The two young girls featured on *The Smashing Pumpkins'* *Siamese Dream* album cover, Ali Langer and Los Angeles Roberts, were child models who met for the first time at the photoshoot in Los Angeles. They are not Siamese twins, as the title might imply. In 2018, Langer and Roberts, now a nurse and an IT professional respectively, reunited to help promote a reformed Smashing Pumpkins and their tour. It has been confirmed that one-time Smashing Pumpkins bassist Nicole Fiorentino is not one of the girls on the cover, despite a claim she made that even fooled Billy Corgan. "In 2018, Ali and Los Angeles got back together to help promote a reformed smashing pumpkins and a tour."

podcast.title: "Tonight, Tonight" Video Awards and Impact
podcast.body: The music video for "Tonight, Tonight" not only garnered numerous awards but also played a crucial role in the commercial success of *Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness*. The double album reached number one on charts worldwide, including Canada, the US, Australia, New Zealand, and Sweden, with total sales of around 10 million copies. "Not only did the video win a bunch of awards, but it helped Melancholy, a double album, reached number one on many of the charts around the world, including Canada, the US, Australia, New Zealand, and Sweden."

podcast.title: "Tonight, Tonight" Video Costume Challenge
podcast.body: The production of The Smashing Pumpkins' "Tonight, Tonight" music video faced a unique challenge regarding costumes. Since James Cameron was simultaneously shooting *Titanic* and had rented "just about every old-timey costume in Hollywood," new, elaborate turn-of-the-century costumes had to be made from scratch for the band. "James Cameron was shooting Titanic at the same time this video was being made, and he just rented just about every old-timey costume in Hollywood, so this meant new clothes had to be made for the smashing pumpkins from scratch."

podcast.body: The Smashing Pumpkins were among the notable alt-rock acts that reunited in the first decade of the 21st century, injecting new, albeit temporary, life into the scene. "In addition, the Pixies, smashing pumpkins...These reunions injected some life into the scene, albeit temporary life."

podcast.title: Acknowledging Judas Priest Influence
podcast.body: Billy Corgan once admitted that some of The Smashing Pumpkins' sound was influenced by Judas Priest. This admission caused "shock and horror" among certain rock fans, illustrating the rigid tribalism of music preferences at the time. "I recall one time when Billy Corgan admitted that some of the smashing pumpkin sound was influenced by Judas Priest and there was shock and horror, treason."

podcast.title: Band Dissolution Reasons
podcast.body: The Smashing Pumpkins exhibited all four common reasons for band separation: members fighting fiercely and hating each other, minor legal disputes and many threats of legal disputes, evident creative differences, and the presence of a charismatic leader (Billy Corgan) who did most of the work while the others lagged behind. "yo creo que cumple todos los requisitos de separación me refiero acabaron todos a hostias odiando se poniendo sacado entre ellos tuvieron disputas legales no muy importante espero tuvieron alguna disputa legal y muchas amenazas de disputas legales bueno a ver las diferencias creativas eran evidentes y luego también pues evidentemente estaba Billy Corgan que era el que hacía prácticamente todo y el resto que estaba un poco resagado entonces yo creo que cumple todos los requisitos de separación de la banda."

podcast.title: Big Muff as Core Sound
podcast.body: The Smashing Pumpkins' existence and distinctive sound are attributed to a specific model of the Big Muff pedal. Electroharmonix even sold a custom orange-painted version described as "all the guitars on Simee's Dream in a box," a clear reference to the band's influential use of the pedal. "And there would not have been a smashing pumpkins if not for a specific model of Big Muff."

podcast.title: Billy Corgan's Consistent Leadership
podcast.body: Billy Corgan has been the only constant member of The Smashing Pumpkins since its formation in 1988, underscoring his singular control over the band, as every other member has either quit or been fired. "This is and always has been Billy Corgan's band. He's been the only constant in the group since 1988."

podcast.body: Billy Corgan continues to be involved with The Smashing Pumpkins "in one form or another," indicating the band's ongoing, albeit evolving, existence. "We still have Billy Corgid in the smashing pumpkins in one form or another."

podcast.body: Billy Corgan was known for his "incredibly despotic" way of working with the band members. "la increíblemente despota forma de trabajar que tenía Bili Corgan con el grupo."

podcast.body: At one point, Billy Corgan attempted to release solo material under The Smashing Pumpkins' name, leading to threats of lawsuits from other members. He eventually released a solo album. "después el disco de suam viene el disco estén solitario de Billikon pero en el que también estaba Jimmy Chamberlain había los artículos que hacían que Billikon estaba intentando sacar material en solo con el nombre de los Ismas in Punkies luego venía que los otros lo iban a denunciar porque no podía hacer eso entonces los acaban solitario."

podcast.title: Bowie's Appreciation for the Smashing Pumpkins
podcast.body: David Bowie was a known fan of the Smashing Pumpkins, acknowledging their importance in the alt-rock era. This mutual respect between Bowie and the new generation of musicians contributed to his enduring influence. "Knowing that Bowie was a fan of the pixies and Irvana and the smashing pumpkins and swayed and a wasis and blur and vice versa, you had to give him respect."

podcast.title: Bridging Rock and Metal
podcast.body: Billy Corgan and The Smashing Pumpkins were part of the movement in the early to middle 90s that "slowly closed that big attitude gap between rock and old school metal." Corgan specifically expressed admiration for bands like AC/DC and Led Zeppelin, contributing to a new open-mindedness within alternative rock. "Then guys like Billy Corgan started saying the same thing. Some of those old ACDC records? Pretty great riffs, man."

podcast.title: Career Decline (late 90s)
podcast.body: Towards the end of the 1990s, The Smashing Pumpkins were noted to have "lost their way," indicating a period of creative or commercial difficulty. "The smashing pumpkins lost their way."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Championing Classic Rock
podcast.body: Billy Corgan of The Smashing Pumpkins publicly championed classic rock groups such as Cheap Trick and Judas Priest. This demonstrates a broad musical appreciation that defies the traditional "pick a side" mentality once prevalent among rock fans. "Billy Corgan of the Smashing Pumpkins champion groups like Cheap Trick and Judas Priest."

podcast.title: Charlie Adams, Influential Teacher
podcast.body: Jimmy Chamberlin's most significant drumming teacher was Charlie Adams, who later went on to work for the New Age musician Yanni. This connection highlights the diverse musical lineage that influenced Chamberlin's development. "His most important teacher was a guy named Charlie Adams, and he would later go on to work for Yanny, you know the new age guy with the stash along here."

podcast.title: D'Arcy Wretzky's Post-Band Activities
podcast.body: The story circulated that D'Arcy quit The Smashing Pumpkins in 1999 to pursue an acting career, though nothing seems to have come of those aspirations. On January 25, 2000, she was arrested on crack cocaine charges in Chicago, found with three bags of crack. She was not formally charged but received a court-ordered drug rehab program. Originally from Michigan, she is believed to be living on her horse farm near Watervillet, Michigan, east of Kalamazoo, where she raises Arabian horses. She also owns three antique shops and is reportedly a trained massage therapist. "The story was that in 1999 Darcy quit the pumpkins to pursue a career in acting. The following year, January 25, 2000, she was busted on crack cocaine charges. Cops on the west side of Chicago found her holding three bags of crack after the car in which she was a passenger made a couple of dumb and illegal uterines. Darcy was arrested but not formally charged. Instead, she received a court ordered drug rehab program."

xref.title: Drug Overdoses and Jonathan Melvoin's Death (1996)
xref.body: Within six weeks of the Smashing Pumpkins' 1996 World Tour beginning, drummer Jimmy Chamberlain and touring keyboardist Jonathan Melvoin overdosed on heroin in Thailand in February, and again in Spain in May, narrowly escaping death. Jonathan Melvoin was subsequently fired but remained with the band until the tour concluded, while Jimmy was placed on "double secret probation." On July 11, 1996, just before two sold-out shows at Madison Square Garden in New York, Jimmy and Jonathan went to the East Village to purchase "red rum," a highly potent form of heroin. At 4 AM the next morning, Jonathan, who was ironically trained as an emergency medical technician, died from an overdose. Jimmy awoke from his stupor and called the police, leading to official statements being given within hours. "Jonathan Melvoin O.D. on heroin in Thailand."

xref.title: Dublin Concert Fatality (1996)
xref.body: During their World Tour for *Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness*, The Smashing Pumpkins played to about 7,000 people at the Point Theatre in Dublin, Ireland, on May 11, 1996. Seventeen-year-old Bernadette O'Brien rushed into the mosh pit and was crushed. Singer Billy Corgan stopped the show twice, first asking the crowd to cease crushing, then at 10:00 PM announcing the gig was over due to O'Brien being "nearly dying." O'Brien died the next day from massive internal injuries caused by the crushing weight. Her friend and two cousins were also injured but recovered. "I'm sorry, we can't play on, the gigs are over. There's a girl who's nearly dying. We, as human beings, cannot play up here while people are getting hurt down there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Jimmy Chamberlain's Firing and Return (1996-1999)
xref.body: Five days after Jonathan Melvoin's death, Billy, James, and Darcy of The Smashing Pumpkins issued a statement announcing their decision to "sever our relationship with our friend and drummer Jimmy Chamberlain." They explained that for nine years they had "battled with Jimmy's struggles with the insidious disease of drug and alcohol addiction," which had "nearly destroyed everything we are and stand for," and confirmed they would "carry on without him." Jimmy was exiled from the band for three years, a period during which the Pumpkins' fortunes began to decline. In an effort to revitalize the band, Jimmy was eventually asked to rejoin, making his return on April 10, 1999, at St Andrews Hall in Detroit, where the band appeared in their familiar lineup for the first time since July 1996. "Today, we are very sorry to tell you that we've decided to sever our relationship with our friend and drummer Jimmy Chamberlain."

xref.title: Tom Verlaine Death (January 28, 2023) – Prostate Cancer, Age 73; Helped CBGB Become Ground Zero for Punk
xref.body: Tom Verlaine co-founded Television and in 1973 helped Hilly Kristal — owner of a scuzzy bar on Bleecker Street in a then-terrible part of New York — to let Television play a Sunday night residency. This decision catalyzed CBGB into becoming ground zero for New York punk and, by chain reaction, the entire international punk movement. Television produced two critically acclaimed albums before breaking up in 1978. Verlaine subsequently collaborated with Patti Smith, worked with James Iha of the Smashing Pumpkins, had a song covered by David Bowie, and was involved in a 1992 Television reunion album. He was scheduled to produce Jeff Buckley's second album — a project ended when Buckley drowned in the Mississippi River in 1997. Verlaine was diagnosed with prostate cancer at some point in the 2000s; it metastasized. He died January 28, 2023, age 73. "That was the catalyst for making CBGB ground zero for the world of New York punk."

xref.body: Stuart Chatwood, the bassist and keyboardist for The Tea Party, was considered a strong candidate for the bass player position in The Smashing Pumpkins, although the opportunity ultimately did not materialize. This reflects his high esteem within the music industry. "for a while he was a strong candidate to be the bass player for the smashing pumpkins but that ended up not working out."

xref.title: Support from Indie Musicians
xref.body: Indie musicians in Chicago and beyond, including producer Steve Albini and a former bandmate of Billy Corgan from a pre-Smashing Pumpkins band, took notice and supported Wesley. The Canadian industrial metal band Monster Voodoo Machine recorded with him, and Eddie Vedder was charmed by his work. "The indie musicians of Chicago and beyond took note, and they took a liking to him."

xref.title: Tibetan Freedom Festival Performer
xref.body: The Smashing Pumpkins were part of the lineup for the first annual Tibetan Freedom Show at Golden Gate Park in San Francisco on July 15, 1996, performing alongside the Beastie Boys and other major acts. "The line up included the Beastie Boys, plus the smashing pumpkins."

xref.title: Tibetan Freedom Festival Performer
xref.body: Bjork performed at the first annual Tibetan Freedom Show in Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, on July 15, 1996, contributing to the festival's lineup which raised awareness for Chinese oppression in Tibet. "The line up included the Beastie Boys, plus the smashing pumpkins, Bjork."

xref.title: Tibetan Freedom Festival Performer

xref.title: Tibetan Freedom Festival Performer
xref.body: The Chili Peppers were part of the extensive lineup for the first annual Tibetan Freedom Festival held on July 15, 1996, in San Francisco, an event organized by Adam Yauch. "The line up included the Beastie Boys, plus the smashing pumpkins, Bjork, Sonic Youth, the Chili Peppers, and more."

xref.title: Touring with Pearl Jam and The Smashing Pumpkins
xref.body: The Red Hot Chili Peppers capitalized on the changing musical landscape by having Pearl Jam and The Smashing Pumpkins open for their "Blood Sugar Sex Magik" tour, creating a powerful triple bill. "The Chili Peppers would later capitalize on this change in mentality by getting both Pearl Jam and The Smashing Pumpkins to open for their tour."
